subject: Nightingale
hook: NIGHTINGALE IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: NIGHTINGALE is not what you think because the bird that has inspired poets for centuries as a female songstress is actually almost exclusively male, and only the unpaired ones sing at night.
angle_support: While historically, female nightingales were assumed to be the ones singing, it is nearly always the males since though females will occasionally sing, only males do it regularly.
Only unpaired males sing regularly at night, and nocturnal song probably serves to attract a mate.
title: The Nightingale’s Midnight Call: It’s a Male’s Song
description: Poets imagined a night‑songstress, but science shows the nightingale’s night music comes from solitary males. Their powerful, hours‑long serenades are courting calls, not lullabies.
narration: NIGHTINGALE IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture a delicate female bird crooning under moonlight, a night‑songstress of poetry. Centuries of verse assumed the female sang, yet field studies show the song is almost always produced by males, and only those without a mate launch their nocturnal concerts, because only solitary males need to broadcast, the night’s melody is a mating call, not a lullaby. While historically female nightingales were assumed to be the singers, research notes that males sing regularly while females only occasionally vocalise. Only unpaired males sing at night, using the darkness to attract a mate. Their nocturnal song can last seven to eight hours without major breaks. Male nightingales boast an average repertoire of 190 distinct song types, with exceptional individuals exceeding 300, delivering whistles, trills, gurgles and a loud crescendo that pierces night silence. So the night’s sweet serenade belongs to a lone male, not a poetic lady, echoing his longing.
